svg.text: EBP = best evidence + clinical expertise + patient values — three legs, one stool.

g.text: P — Population (\"in post-op adults…\") · I — Intervention (\"…does early mobilisation…\") ·
C — Comparison (\"…vs bed rest…\") · O — Outcome (\"…cut DVT/pneumonia?\") → searchable,
answerable, auditable. Add T (time) where apt: \"…within 48 hours?\"
APPRAISE (3 questions, 3 minutes): 1 VALID? (right patients? randomised/blinded?
follow-up complete? harms reported?) → 2 BIG? (effect size + confidence intervals —
statistical ≠ clinical significance) → 3 USEFUL HERE? (my patients? my resources? my
setting? — a US ICU trial may not fit a Ghana district ward). Red flags: tiny samples,
industry-only funding undisclosed, surrogate outcomes (\"lowers X\" ≠ \"saves lives\"), no
harms reported, predatory journals. Trust pyramid: Ghana STG/protocols + WHO →
systematic reviews → RCTs → cohorts → expert opinion → \"we've always done it\".
BARRIERS + BEATERS: no time (journal club 30 min/month, one paper, ward-relevant) →
no access (WHO HINARI, open access, library, protocols first) → no skill (appraisal buddies,
CPD courses) → \"doctors decide\" (nurses own nursing care evidence: pressure care,
falls, feeding, education) → no authority (pilot small, audit, present data — data persuades
where rank resists). Tradition kills quietly: routine episiotomy, NPO-from-midnight,
saline-for-all — EBP retired each where evidence spoke. \"We've always done it\" is
history, not justification: honour experience, obey evidence, blend with expertise.
Journal club recipe: 1 paper + 3 appraisal Qs + \"what changes Monday?\" + audit + date.
Exam line: \"ask answerably, acquire hierarchically, appraise skeptically, apply jointly, assess honestly.\"
